name: yolo-dag
description: Turns an ambiguous request into a reviewed, executed, integrated branch: /brainstorm asks one question up front — plan-only run, or full run? — then resolves ambiguity (autonomously, asking only when high-stakes) and hands off to the orchestrator, which routes to the relevant domain specialists, closes each with a 3-reviewer/1-consolidator review loop, merges and reconciles them into one build spec, and decomposes it into tasks designed to be independent — shared boundaries written out as contracts both sides code against, a dependency edge only where the ordering couldn't be designed away, and every file owned by exactly one task. A full run then implements without asking again; a plan-only run stops at that boundary and waits. Execution runs in user-paced passes of worktree-isolated workers: one question per pass — how many tasks in parallel — with the orchestrator picking an independent set itself, sending flagged work back to its own worker to rework, and merging each approved task onto the run's integration branch, finishing with a whole-suite run plus an acceptance review of the assembled diff against the original request. Every phase persists to .dag/runs/<run-id>/ so an interrupted run resumes instead of restarting.
